overview.description: 9-5-2: trick-taking game; name may refer to card ranks or deal (e.g. 9, 5, 2 cards). Trump and follow suit; point or trick count to win. Played in India and elsewhere.

history.origins: Related to Sergeant Major (RAF: 3p, 16 cards, targets 8-5-3). 9-5-2 and its close relative 3-2-5 (Teen Do Panch) are played in India, Pakistan and Nepal using a reduced pack with trick quotas.
timeline: 20th century: Documented as a South Asian quota trick-taking game related to Sergeant Major and 3-2-5 (Teen Do Panch).

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.

rules.objective: Meet your trick quota (e.g. 9, 5, or 2 tricks depending on position); overtricks score, shortfall penalised.
rules.gameplay: Trick-taking; dealer names trump (or no trump). Follow suit; trump if void. Each player has a target number of tricks (e.g. 9 for dealer, 5 for left, 2 for right). Pay or receive stakes per trick above/below target.
keyRules: Dealer chooses trump; kitty in some variants
Pay/receive per trick above or below quota

strategy.basic: 9-5-2: follow rules; strategy depends on variant.
strategy.intermediate: Count cards or points; adapt to variant.

list.name: Clockwise Deal and Play
list.description: Deal and play can proceed clockwise instead of counter-clockwise, with the player to dealer's left taking the higher trick quota, choosing trumps, and leading to the first trick while the player to dealer's right takes the lower quota.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Engine overrides for rotating deal direction and swapping trick quotas by seat are not modeled yet; implementers should apply this variation from the textual rules.

list.name: Sevens as Permanent Trumps
list.description: In some circles both Sevens are permanent trumps: the 7 of hearts is the highest trump, followed by the 7 of spades, then the remaining cards of the chosen trump suit in their usual order.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Permanent-trump treatment of the Sevens affects trick resolution but is not reflected in engine overrides; implementers must handle this ranking rule explicitly.
